title: Transcriptomics data: pointing the way to subclassification and personalized medicine in systemic lupus erythematosus.
authors: Hubbard, Erika L; Grammer, Amrie C; Lipsky, Peter E
one_liner_zh: 该文综述基于转录组数据对SLE患者进行亚型分类和精准医学研究，虽涉及转录因子活性推断，但核心是疾病分型而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，且无AI/物理模拟方法聚焦于TF-DNA结合机制。
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To summarize recent studies stratifying SLE patients into subgroups based on gene expression profiling and suggest future improvements for employing transcriptomic data to foster precision medicine. RECENT FINDINGS: Bioinformatic & machine learning pipelines have been employed to dissect the transcriptomic heterogeneity of lupus patients and identify more homogenous subgroups. Some examples include the use of unsupervised random forest and k-means clustering to separate adult SLE patients into seven clusters and hierarchical clustering of single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) of immune cells yielding four clusters in a cohort of adult SLE and pediatric SLE participants. Random forest classification of bulk RNA-seq data from sorted blood cells enabled prediction of high or low disease activity in European and Asian SLE patients. Inferred transcription factor activity stratified adult and pediatric SLE into two subgroups. SUMMARY: Several different endotypes of SLE patients with differing molecular profiles have been reported but a global consensus of clinically actionable groups has not been reached. Moreover, heterogeneity between datasets, reproducibility of predictions as well as the most effective classification approach have not been resolved. Nevertheless, gene expression-based precision medicine remains an attractive option to subset lupus patients.
abstract_zh: 综述目的：总结近期基于基因表达谱对系统性红斑狼疮（SLE）患者进行亚组分层的研究，并提出未来利用转录组数据促进精准医学的改进建议。近期发现：已采用生物信息学和机器学习流程来解析狼疮患者的转录组异质性，并识别更同质的亚组。一些例子包括使用无监督随机森林和k-means聚类将成人SLE患者分为七个簇，以及通过免疫细胞单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）的层次聚类在成人SLE和儿童SLE参与者队列中产生四个簇。对分选血细胞的批量RNA-seq数据进行随机森林分类，能够预测欧洲和亚洲SLE患者的高或低疾病活动度。推断的转录因子活性将成人和儿童SLE分为两个亚组。总结：已报道了具有不同分子谱的多种SLE患者内型，但尚未达成全球共识的临床可操作分组。此外，数据集之间的异质性、预测的可重复性以及最有效的分类方法尚未解决。尽管如此，基于基因表达的精准医学仍是细分狼疮患者的一个有吸引力的选择。
